Remark[edit]

This problem is a reduced version of 1985 AIME Problem 12, changing steps into steps.

This problem is also similar to 2003 AIME II Problem 13.

~isabelchen \begin{solution} At each hop, the cricket must move to one of the other three leaves with equal probability. Thus the total number of possible hop sequences of length is \[ 3^4 = 81. \]

We count the number of \emph{favorable} sequences in which the cricket is on the starting leaf after the fourth hop.

---

\textbf{Case 1: The cricket returns to the starting leaf exactly once.}

Since the cricket cannot remain on the same leaf, the only way for it to return exactly once and still end at the starting leaf is for the return to occur on the \emph{fourth hop}.

\begin{itemize} \item Hop 1: From the starting leaf, there are choices. \item Hop 2: The cricket is on a non-starting leaf; it must avoid returning, so there are choices. \item Hop 3: Again, the cricket is on a non-starting leaf and must avoid returning, giving choices. \item Hop 4: The cricket must return to the starting leaf, which is favorable choice. \end{itemize}

Thus the number of favorable sequences in Case 1 is \[ 3 \cdot 2 \cdot 2 \cdot 1 = 12. \]

---

\textbf{Case 2: The cricket returns to the starting leaf exactly twice.}

With four hops and no ability to stay in place, the only possible return pattern is \[ \text{start} \to \text{other} \to \text{start} \to \text{other} \to \text{start}, \] which corresponds to hops and being returns.

\begin{itemize} \item Hop 1: From the starting leaf, there are choices. \item Hop 2: The cricket must return to the starting leaf ( choice). \item Hop 3: From the starting leaf, there are again choices. \item Hop 4: The cricket must return to the starting leaf ( choice). \end{itemize}

Thus the number of favorable sequences in Case 2 is \[ 3 \cdot 1 \cdot 3 \cdot 1 = 9. \]

---

\textbf{Conclusion.}

The total number of favorable sequences is \[ 12 + 9 = 21. \] Therefore, the desired probability is \[ \frac{21}{81} = \boxed{\frac{7}{27}}. \] \end{solution}
